h2: Ultrasonic testing around Dallas and Fort Worth: boilers, gas gathering and power plants
html:
Ultrasonic testing around Dallas and Fort Worth: boilers, gas gathering and power plants

In Dallas–Fort Worth, ultrasonic testing is booked most often for thickness readings that support a boiler or piping inspection, for weld examination on fabricated and repaired equipment, and for wall-loss measurement on Barnett Shale gathering systems. Atlantis sends UT technicians from Houston to North Texas sites, with every procedure and report reviewed by an ASNT NDT Level III.

Boilers under the TDLR program. Texas regulates boilers through the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation, which oversees about 54,000 of them. Certificate inspections fall every 12, 24 or 36 months depending on the boiler type, and are carried out by commissioned inspectors employed by an Authorized Inspection Agency, usually the insurer, or by TDLR deputy inspectors where a boiler is uninsured. The commissioned inspector makes the call; UT supplies the evidence, such as tube and drum thickness, header and economizer wall loss, and examination of weld repairs. Atlantis performs that NDE. It is not an Authorized Inspection Agency and does not carry out certificate inspections. Booking the readings a few weeks before the certificate date gives the inspector measured data instead of a list of open questions.

Gas gathering and midstream. The Barnett Shale lies beneath Fort Worth, and Railroad Commission figures put about 2,700 wells in Tarrant County alone by 2011, each tied in by gathering pipe. Dallas is also headquarters to Energy Transfer and Atmos Energy. For UT, that means thickness surveys on compressor and meter-station piping, dead legs and low points where water collects, and wall measurement at excavations. Intrastate lines answer to the Railroad Commission of Texas; interstate lines answer to PHMSA.

Power generation. Comanche Peak's two pressurized water reactors at Glen Rose are examined under ASME Section XI, where UT procedures and personnel must pass performance demonstration before they are used. That is a specialist nuclear program. Outside it, combined-cycle and industrial plants across the region use UT on HRSG tubing, steam and feedwater piping, and deaerator and heater shells.

Typical North Texas UT scopes:

  • Boiler tube, drum and header thickness ahead of a TDLR certificate inspection
  • Station piping, dead legs and injection points on gathering and compression systems
  • Shear-wave or phased array weld examination on new vessels and structural steel to ASME Section VIII or AWS D1.1
  • Automated corrosion mapping on vessel shells and tank walls where spot readings would miss localized loss
  • TOFD and PAUT in place of radiography where the construction code and the client allow it

The method, its detection limits and what a report contains are on the ultrasonic testing page. Weld examination with encoded data is covered by phased array inspection services, and grid or C-scan wall mapping by automated UT and corrosion mapping. Vessel owners working through an API 510 program can see how the NDE fits on the pressure vessel inspection page. Thickness data only becomes a trend when every reading is tied to the same location each time, which is what the Atlantis ERP reporting module is built to keep. Technicians looking for a course rather than a crew should go to UT training or the Dallas NDT training page. For site work, send the equipment list, drawings and target dates through the Dallas–Fort Worth UT request.
